trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Number 2 is only reachable this way.
Number 3 is only reachable this way.
Number 4 is only reachable this way.
Going down-right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down-left.
I can't rule out left or down-left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: left.
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
Going up-left would turn number 8 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes left.
Going up-right would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going right would turn number 10 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Going up-left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,-2). So the line goes left.

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going up-left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,-2); going up-right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So my guess (left from cell (0,1)) was wrong, so the line must go down-left.
Number 5 is only reachable this way.
Number 6 is only reachable this way.
The line must go right: up-right is number 8, which comes later.
Going up-left would turn number 8 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Going up-right would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going right would turn number 10 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Going up-left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,-2). So the line goes left.
Going up-left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,-2). So the line goes up-right.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up-left.
The line must go down-left: left is number 14, which comes later.
Going up-left would turn number 14 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going down-right would turn number 17 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Number 20 is only reachable this way.
Number 21 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would wall in number 23, the last number; going to number 22 would leave both cell (-1,1) and cell (-3,2) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down-left.
Cell (-3,3) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
